working_title: Beyond Royal Portrush: Northern Ireland's Causeway Coast Courses Worth Adding to Your Itinerary
angle: Royal Portrush is the obvious bucket-list tick on Northern Ireland's Causeway Coast, but at £420 a round in 2026 and tee times that evaporate fast, most visitors need a Plan B. This post makes the case for the supporting cast — Portstewart Strand, Castlerock Mussenden, and Ardglass — as genuinely outstanding rounds in their own right, not just fillers.
research_notes:
- Royal Portrush (Dunluce Links) green fee 2026: £420 per person, April 1–October 31. Valley Links is £200pp for the same period. Visitors must be members of a recognised club; handicap certificates may be requested. No play on Wednesdays. Source: royalportrushgolfclub.com.
- Royal Portrush designed by Harry Colt; updated by Martin Ebert. Par 71, 7,381 yards (Open Championship layout). Hosted The Open in 1951, 2019, and 2025 (won by Scottie Scheffler at –17). Course features the famous 'Calamity Corner.'
- Royal County Down: green fees rose 18% to £425 for 2025; similarly inaccessible for casual visitors without planning well ahead.
- Portstewart Golf Club (Strand Course): widely cited as one of the best links in Ireland; known for towering sand dunes and dramatic views. No confirmed 2026 green fee found — describe in general terms only.
- Castlerock Golf Club (Mussenden Links): 18-hole links plus 9-hole Bann Course. Visitor green fees 2026: £175 (April and October), £250 (May–September). Established 1901; extended by Ben Sayers of North Berwick in 1908. Named for nearby Mussenden Temple on the clifftops. Described by visitors as 'often forgotten' next to Portrush and Portstewart but 'worth a visit.' Previously won an award for Best Value course in Northern Ireland per Golfshake reviews. The course is bounded by the beach, the River Bann, and the Belfast–Derry railway line.
- Ardglass Golf Club: cliff-top links on Northern Ireland's southeast coast; historic clubhouse in a building dating to the 13th/15th century (sources vary slightly — describe as a historic fortified structure, do not state a precise century). Once bypassed by visitors heading to RCD/Portrush; now widely cited as a must-play add-on to Royal County Down. Peak-season green fee rose to £220 for 2025 (most recent confirmed figure — note this is 2025 data; confirm current rate with club before booking). Reinvestment from visitor revenue has improved course condition year on year.
- Northern Ireland has over 90 courses; temperate climate means golf is playable most of the year.
- Post-2019 Open economic impact on Northern Ireland golf tourism was significant; visitor green fees at top courses more than doubled since pre-2019 Open era. Tee-time scarcity at the flagship courses is now a genuine logistical challenge.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club also mentioned in research as an emerging lower-cost alternative on the northeast coast — could be flagged as an 'one to watch' without over-committing to detail not in the research.
- Practical logistics: most visitors base themselves in Portrush, Portstewart, or Bushmills — short drives to the Causeway Coast courses. Ardglass is on the southeast coast, about an hour from Portrush cluster, better paired with a Royal County Down day.
- No specific Portstewart 2026 green fee found in research — do not invent a figure.
